headword: ご{祝儀袋|しゅうぎぶくろ}

definitions.gloss: gift money envelope; congratulatory money envelope
definitions.explanation: A decorated envelope used to present monetary gifts at celebrations, especially weddings. Features ornamental paper cords (mizuhiki) and is sold at stationery stores and convenience stores.

examples.japanese: ご{祝儀袋|しゅうぎぶくろ}を{買|か}いに{行|い}く。
examples.english: I'm going to buy a gift money envelope.

examples.japanese: ご{祝儀袋|しゅうぎぶくろ}に{三万円|さんまんえん}{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put 30,000 yen in the gift money envelope.

examples.japanese: {結婚式|けっこんしき}に{出席|しゅっせき}するので、ご{祝儀袋|しゅうぎぶくろ}の{書|か}き{方|かた}を{調|しら}べた。
examples.english: Since I'm attending a wedding, I looked up how to write on a gift money envelope.

notes:
A compound of ご{祝儀|しゅうぎ} (congratulatory gift, tip) and {袋|ぶくろ} (bag, envelope). These special envelopes are an essential part of Japanese gift-giving culture, particularly for weddings.

CULTURAL NOTE:
For weddings, the standard gift amount is {三万円|さんまんえん} (30,000 yen) for friends and colleagues. Odd numbers are preferred because they cannot be evenly divided (symbolizing the couple staying together). The envelope should be written with the giver's full name using a brush pen ({筆|ふで}ペン). Different styles of {水引|みずひき} (decorative cords) are used for different occasions — a tied bow for weddings indicates a one-time celebration.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ご{祝儀袋|しゅうぎぶくろ}に{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}く — to write one's name on the envelope
- ご{祝儀袋|しゅうぎぶくろ}にお{金|かね}を{入|い}れる — to put money in the envelope
- ご{祝儀袋|しゅうぎぶくろ}の{選|えら}び{方|かた} — how to choose the right envelope

RELATED WORDS:
- ご{祝儀|しゅうぎ} — congratulatory gift money; the money itself
- {水引|みずひき} — decorative paper cords on gift envelopes
- {不祝儀袋|ぶしゅうぎぶくろ} — condolence money envelope; the counterpart used at funerals
- {香典袋|こうでんぶくろ} — incense money envelope; another term for funeral gift envelopes

cross_references.label: decorative paper cords on gift envelopes
